newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh soldier, police killed by rebels.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh soldier, police killed by rebels.

text.p: Suspected tribal rebels shot dead a soldier and three policemen in a series of attacks on Saturday in the Chittagong Hill Tracts of southwestern Bangladesh, security officials said.
Officials said the attacks were an attempt to torpedo the current peace process seeking an end to the decades-old insurgency in the Hill districts.

Security sources have blamed a hardline group within the Shanti Bahini (peace force) opposing a peace intiative taken by the government and the Parbatya Chittagram Jana Sanghati Samity (PCJSS), the political wing of the Bahini, to end the rebellion.
Officials say the two sides made progress in settling the dispute at a meeting in the capital Dhaka last month. Another meeting is due on March 12.

Tribal insurgents have been fighting a bush war for autonomy for 5,500 sq miles (14,200 sq km) of hill tracts bordering India and Burma. They also want some 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers expelled from the area.
Officials say more than 8,500 rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency since 1973.
